newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA SAYS NO TAX RELIEFS IN GOVERNMENT PAY HIKES.
newsitem.headline: INDIA SAYS NO TAX RELIEFS IN GOVERNMENT PAY HIKES.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, facing protests from disgruntled government employees over pay rises, told parliament on Friday that the government had no plans to exempt their salaries from taxation.

"The government does not propose to keep pay and other allowances out of the tax net. The government does not accept the principle that pay and allowances should not be taxed," Chidambaram said in response to a lawmaker's question.
The government is holding back the implementation of the 135-billion-rupee plan for pay increases, which were approved by the cabinet last month, until differences are ironed out with staff unions.
The pay rises, which would affect 5.2 million employees, had been scheduled to start this month.
"The cabinet secretary is meeting the representatives of the joint consultative machinery, and I hope all the issues will be resolved in view of the available resources," Chidambaram said.
The cabinet secretary, T.S.R. Subramaniam, is India's most senior civil servant.

Subramaniam said earlier this week that the government was holding back implementation of the recommendations of a high-powered pay panel following differences with some unions which said the planned pay increases created large disparities between senior and junior government staff.
The Fifth Pay Commission submitted its report in January.
"We think the Pay Commission has acted on a fair manner," Chidambaram said.
"The government has met most of the aspirations of the government employees. Even then we have entered into consultations with the representatives of the employees."

"While responding to demands for increased benefit to the employees, we must expect them to bring about efficiency in their work culture. We are not getting the best from our employees," Chidambaram said.
